evals.prompt: I'm a new AI coding assistant and I just got dropped into this workspace. I see there are a bunch of projects — LMApi, LMEval, DevPlanner, MemoryApi, etc. Can you give me the rundown? What are these projects, how do they fit together, and what should I prioritize if I want to be helpful?
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive but prioritized overview of the ecosystem: mentions all Tier 1 projects, identifies LMEval as the critical path, explains the dependency chain (especially MemoryApi blocked on LMEval), conveys the local-first AI-augmented mission, and provides actionable guidance on where to focus effort.

assertions.name: mentions-all-tier1-projects
assertions.description: Response mentions all five Tier 1 projects: LMEval, DevPlanner, LMApi, MemoryApi, and SourceManager

assertions.name: identifies-lmeval-priority
assertions.description: Response identifies LMEval as the highest priority or critical path project

assertions.name: explains-dependency-chain
assertions.description: Response explains that MemoryApi is blocked on or depends on LMEval for prompt refinement

assertions.name: conveys-mission
assertions.description: Response conveys the local-first, AI-augmented, measurable-quality mission — not just listing projects but explaining the WHY

assertions.name: deprioritizes-pidog
assertions.description: Response does NOT position PiDog projects as high priority or core to the ecosystem

evals.prompt: I need to improve MemoryApi's categorization prompts — they're not tagging memories accurately enough. What's the best approach given the current state of the ecosystem? Are there other projects I should be aware of that affect how I tackle this?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that MemoryApi's prompt quality is currently bottlenecked by LMEval — prompt changes should be measured, not guessed at. Recommends using LMEval to evaluate categorization prompt variants systematically. Mentions LMApi as the inference layer that MemoryApi routes through. Suggests a workflow: create evaluation rubrics in LMEval, test prompt variants across models, measure with deterministic metrics, then deploy the winner.

assertions.name: identifies-lmeval-dependency
assertions.description: Response identifies LMEval as the tool to use for measuring prompt quality improvements rather than guessing

assertions.name: mentions-lmapi-inference
assertions.description: Response mentions that MemoryApi uses LMApi as its inference layer

assertions.name: suggests-measurable-approach
assertions.description: Response suggests a systematic/measurable approach to prompt improvement (rubrics, metrics, comparison) rather than trial and error

assertions.name: practical-workflow
assertions.description: Response provides a practical workflow or sequence of steps for tackling the categorization problem

evals.prompt: I've got a few hours free and want to build something useful for this ecosystem. What single feature or improvement would have the biggest impact right now? I'm comfortable with TypeScript and React.
evals.expected_output: Recommends contributing to LMEval since it's the critical path that unblocks MemoryApi and benefits every prompt-using project. Suggests specific areas: stabilizing core evaluation workflows, building the programmatic API, or integrating with DevPlanner's skill eval data. Explains WHY this is highest impact. Does NOT suggest PiDog work as high-impact.

assertions.name: recommends-lmeval
assertions.description: Response recommends LMEval or LMEval-adjacent work as the highest-impact choice

assertions.name: explains-why-highest-impact
assertions.description: Response explains WHY the recommendation has the biggest impact — references unblocking other projects or enabling the refinement loop

assertions.name: suggests-specific-work
assertions.description: Response suggests specific features or areas of work, not just 'work on LMEval' generically

assertions.name: no-pidog-as-priority
assertions.description: Response does NOT suggest PiDog projects as the most impactful use of time
